subject: Tiered-storage spillover & runbook handoff with Pinecone and EdgeOps
messages:
From: Kate Lin <kate@pinecone.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel@edgeops.co>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tiered storage spillover — readiness check

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Following up with the ops team — Daniel from EdgeOps and I put together a short checklist that we think will help avoid noisy failovers when the S3 cold-tier spillover is triggered for heavy query windows.

High level items we want to align on:
- Read-only mirroring window expectations (15 min target)
- Backoff policy when Pinecone returns 429 under cold-node pressure
- Auth rotation approach for the temporary S3 credentials Redwood will use for backfill/rehydration

I've attached a first-draft runbook and a small CSV with the credential placeholders so your infra team can validate names/paths. Can your team confirm if the runbook section on prefix-based eviction matches your current prefix hashing? If not, we'll adjust.

Daniel will be on the thread for operational details — he's suggested a short canary during the Tuesday maintenance window (06/22).

Best,
Kate Lin
Partner Sales, Pinecone
[kate@pinecone.io]

Attachment: redwood-pinecone-spillover-runbook-v1.pdf (pdf, 320 KB)
Attachment: s3-credentials-stub.csv (csv, 1 KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Kate Lin <kate@pinecone.io>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel@edgeops.co>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered storage spillover & runbook handoff with Pinecone and EdgeOps

Thanks Kate — useful doc, appreciate the detail. Quick notes from our side after an infra skim: 

- Prefix hashing: we do a 2-part hash (customer_id + recent_window_id) which means eviction tends to be localized per-tenant; the runbook's assumption of tenant-wide prefix eviction is slightly off. We'll mark the runbook where to change.
- 429/backoff: we prefer exponential backoff with jitter up to 30s and an opt-in fast-path for premium customers. Can you surface how Pinecone signals that S3 spillover is the cause versus in-cluster memory pressure?
- Credentials: security prefers short-lived STS tokens over static CSVs — the CSV is fine as a placeholder but we'll exchange a KMS-backed STS workflow in the final runbook.

Action items I propose now: 
1) Ben — can you confirm the rehydration job in BatchRunner supports per-tenant rate limiting and whether it respects 429 headers?
2) Laura — can you update the runbook text for prefix hashing (I'll pin the exact wording after Ben confirms)?
3) Kate/Daniel — if we do the canary on Tue (06/22) morning, what's your recommended traffic window and rollback triggers?

If we're aligned I'll put a short MOP into Confluence and loop in our SRE on-call for the canary.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partner Operations, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Hannah — quick tech confirmation after a run with BatchRunner: 

- Rehydration supports per-tenant rate limiting via token-bucket and will honor 429 HTTP response codes when present. We currently parse Retry-After headers; adding jitter was straightforward and I'll include a config knob for the premium fast-path.
- We don't have a Pinecone-specific header today that explicitly flags "spillover to S3". Pinecone's side suggested using an augmented metric stream (cluster.evictions and spillover.count) surfaced in the partner telemetry feed. If Pinecone can expose spillover.count in their telemetry, we can wire a guard that slows rehydration when that metric trends up.

Attaching my proposed CLI snippet for the rehydrate job plus a short patch for Retry-After backoff semantics. If Kate/Daniel can confirm the telemetry name, I can push the change by EOD Monday.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: batchrunner-rehydrate-sample.patch (txt, 3 KB)

From: Daniel Park <daniel@edgeops.co>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Kate Lin <kate@pinecone.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered storage spillover & runbook handoff with Pinecone and EdgeOps

Thanks all — quick operational answers: 

- Canary window: Tue 06/22 02:00–04:00 PT (low traffic) with a 15-minute progressive ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> stop if any of the rollback triggers fire.
- Rollback triggers (suggested): repeated 5xx to Pinecone control plane > 1% over 5 min, spillover.count spike > 3x baseline, tail latency for queries > 250ms p95 for 10 minutes.
- For credentials we'll run a short-lived STS exchange — EdgeOps will generate the role and we will consume via our STS refresher. We'll handle the CSV only as an initial mapping.

I'll schedule a 30-minute dry-run call Monday 06/21 09:00 PT to walk through the steps (validation, traffic split, monitoring dashboards). Let me know if that time conflicts.

— Daniel Park
Ops Lead, EdgeOps Consulting
daniel@edgeops.co
